newsitem.title: UK: Zambian cobalt airfreighted to Europe.
newsitem.headline: Zambian cobalt airfreighted to Europe.

text.p: DAS Air Cargo said it has been moving around 100 tonnes of cobalt a week from Zambia since March and expects to continue doing so into May, the carrier's commercial director, Andy Leslie told Reuters.

"We've moved 36 tonnes on a scheduled weekly McDonnell Douglas DC-10-30 freighter out of Lusaka with the remainder handled by two extra Boeing 707 freighter flights, each carrying 36 tonnes," he added.
"We have two weekly shipments of cobalt confirmed throughout May, with one carried on the DC-10 and the rest on a 707, giving a weekly total of just over 70 tonnes.
A European cobalt source confirmed the shipments and said most was destined for Antwerp and Rotterdam.
Key reasons for choosing airfreight for moving cobalt were that deliveries were late and losses of metal had been encountered when it was moved by rail from Zambia to Dar-es-Salaam, he added.
"The fact is that it is quicker and cheaper in such circumstances to use airfreight," he said.
DAS' Leslie said that two flights were cancelled by the shipper and one was delayed due to Gatwick airport being closed as a result of a security alert.

The airline is UK-managed but operates four Boeing 707 freighters in addition to the DC-10. A second DC-10 has been acquired and after conversion to a freighter will enter service late this year. -Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
